rubric_items.reason: All six acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-11, with L20 split into page size, sort, search and Next appointment. The 'long time' goal is listed under Out of scope with a reason.
Most REQs are atomic and checkable. REQ-8 combines two checks: the existing sort order is kept, and no Last visit sort option is added.
Every known status is backed by a ticket line, a baseline or glossary anchor, or an IDE answer (A-01..A-04). No invented values were found.
No clash between the ticket and the baseline. Time zone (Asia/Kolkata) and the medical-history rule both agree with the ticket.
The questions were few, offered real options, and all were answered in the IDE. None are left open or blocking needlessly.
Plain language. Glossary statuses (Completed, Cancelled, No-show, Scheduled) are used consistently. The missing glossary terms are flagged.

findings.text: REQ-8 joins two separately testable behaviours: the current sort order is kept, and Last visit is not added as a sort option (from A-03). They are closely linked, but a tester checks them separately.

cites.quote: The patient list keeps its current `sort order`; Last visit is display-only and is not added as a sort option.

findings.suggested_fix: Split into REQ-8 (current sort order kept, citing ticket L20) and a new REQ (Last visit is not a sort option, citing A-03).
